title: Sunny Finds a Rainbow | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka wakes just after rain and finds a rainbow arching over the whole bush at sunset — and stands underneath it feeling like the most colourful thing in the world. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The rain had just stopped.

Sunny stepped out from under the tree where she had been sheltering and sniffed. The air smelled completely different after rain — washed and green and new, as if everything had been rinsed and set out again.

She looked up.

There it was.

A full rainbow, arching across the whole sky. Not half a rainbow or a faint stripe — a complete arc, red on the outside curving all the way through orange and yellow and green and blue and into violet, planted firmly in the bush on both sides. So bright after the grey of the rain that it looked impossible.

She walked out into the open to see all of it.

The rainbow sat there patiently while she walked toward it. Of course, it moved as she moved — it was everywhere and nowhere, painted in the sky — but she kept walking anyway, feeling like she was moving through something.

Under the rainbow the air felt different. Slightly softer. Slightly lit.

She stood in the middle of the clearing and spread her paws wide.

She thought: I am standing under a rainbow. This is one of the best things that has ever happened.

The rainbow held itself in the wet sky, patient and enormous.

She sat down in the damp grass and watched until it slowly, gently faded.

Even the fading was beautiful.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, rainbow. Goodnight, little one.
